findings.premise: The proposed client wiring defines a complete displayed-version handshake for insrc_present.
findings.evidence: The MCP input requires versions already supplied by its caller. The existing chat path invokes '.declared(ev.present)' asynchronously from a tool-call event; ReviewPresenterDeps.open returns void, and declared returns only opened/notPending/unreadable. There is no return channel carrying the displayed version into that MCP invocation. Naming 'review-presenter relay' does not define such a channel, its ordering, or how external MCP hosts obtain versions. Without it, the proposed missing-version refusal prevents presentation from completing. findings.action: Specify a callable preparation/read surface or an explicit display acknowledgement protocol, including version acquisition, correlation, token ownership and completion ordering. Include the chat host and transport changes needed to implement it. The prose adequately states per-artifact token ownership/cardinality; the missing interaction contract needs completion, not merely an optional diagram. No visual definitions or companion files are supplied to verify.

findings.premise: The versions-in/tokens-out protocol migration is covered while preserving usable public contracts.
findings.evidence: The canonical shipped steering explicitly instructs 'insrc_present({ documents: [...] })' followed by 'insrc_workflow_approve({ artifactPath })'. The design makes the former return notPending without versions and the latter refuse without tokens, but excludes steering and guide updates from its change sites. Existing present-dispatch tests likewise assert successful documents-only requests. Keeping the response array names does not preserve these request semantics. findings.premise: Locking review publication makes JSON and markdown publication fail closed.
findings.evidence: run-artifact.ts, findings.ts and verdicts.ts write the new review into JSON before writing markdown. writeAtomic atomically renames one file; it provides no multi-file transaction. If the markdown write fails or the process exits between writes, the new JSON review can coexist with the old displayed markdown. Preserving the presentation fields and checking only the markdown contentVersion can then leave an old token valid against an unpublished review result. The design specifies no incomplete-publication state, rollback or recovery check. [files: src/workflow/review/run-artifact.ts, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/findings.ts, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts, src/workflow/storage.ts]
findings.action: Define crash-safe publication or a recoverable publication marker that blocks presentation/approval until JSON and markdown agree. Specify failure handling and add fault injection between the two writes.

findings.premise: Accepting a rejected non-AMD artifact in recordPresentations enables the stated IDE re-approval recovery.
findings.evidence: handleReviewDecision rejects approve/reject before reaching approveWorkflowTarget whenever state !== 'pending', returning 'it is already rejected, not awaiting review'. The proposed change to this handler only forwards presentToken, and recordPresentations' specified writes do not clear rejectedAt. pendingArtifacts also continues excluding rejected records, so pending-list-based client discovery cannot reopen them. findings.action: Specify how rejected artifacts are located and reopened, and update the reviewDecision state guard to permit the intended token-validated recovery. Preserve AMD terminal rejection and test the actual IDE path.

summary.prose: Token+contentVersion-bound present-before-approve in the daemon, with a complete handshake and per-artifact batch tokens: insrc_present takes each document name plus the contentVersion the client displayed and returns the pinned { presented, notPending } arrays plus a per-artifact token map; every approval call (single, epicHash batch, reviewDecision, TUI, AMD) carries the matching token(s), validated under a per-artifact lock against a fresh reread (token equality, unconsumed, TTL, current render === presentedContentVersion), then consumed. Review publication is bound to an input contentVersion snapshot verified under the publication lock (mismatch → review restarts). All writers — approve, reject, every review publication, questions, resolve-comment, feedback, synthesize, tracker meta, standalone BUILD record, present stamp, AMD transitions — serialize under the same lock with fresh rereads, preserving presentation fields.
